evals.name: oauth-sign-in-full
evals.prompt: Can you explain to me how 'Sign in with Google' actually works? I want a visual explainer page, full visual please, I'm going to share it with my team.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML explainer in full interactive mode: a one-minute short version stating that the app never sees the password, a plain-language how-it-works layer with diagrams and self-checks, an animated walkthrough of the sign-in (on screen and the messages behind it), interactive elements that make the reader think, and a deep dive with the extra protections and sources.
assertions: Produces exactly one HTML file
Self-contained: no external scripts, stylesheets or images (a web-font link is allowed)
The opening screen states the answer as a sentence (not a topic title like 'OAuth explained')
Opens with a short management-style summary: the answer plus at most four takeaways, readable in about a minute
Has distinct layers: a short version, a plain-language how-it-works part, and a deeper detail part
Every abbreviation is spelled out at its first appearance
Technical terms (for example access token, scope, redirect) are explained in plain words
Has an animated, step-by-step demonstration of the sign-in that the reader can pause or step through
Has at least three interactive elements that require the reader to think (guess, order, slide, explore)
Has at least three self-check questions
Animations respect the reader's reduced-motion setting
No emoji used as icons or decoration
No horizontal overflow or overlapping text at 1280px and 400px widths
Accurate: never says the app receives or stores the user's password, and explains the code-for-token exchange

evals.name: git-rebase-baseline
evals.prompt: I never understood git rebase vs merge. make me an explainer page, keep it simple
evals.expected_output: A calm, simple HTML explainer: the answer first (what each does and when to use which), diagrams of the commit history before and after a merge and a rebase, the risk of rebasing shared history, a step-by-step demonstration of the commands, and self-checks, with no heavy interactive extras.
assertions: Produces exactly one HTML file
The opening states when to use rebase versus merge, before any background
Shows the commit history before and after, as diagrams, for both merge and rebase
Explains the risk of rebasing commits that others already have (rewriting shared history)
Shows the exact commands to run, in order (for example git switch feature, then git rebase main)
Has at least two self-check questions
Every abbreviation is spelled out at its first appearance
Respects 'keep it simple': under about 700 words in total, and no deep-dive section
Kept simple: no sentence longer than 28 words
Animations respect the reader's reduced-motion setting
No emoji used as icons or decoration
No horizontal overflow or overlapping text at 1280px and 400px widths

evals.name: repo-pipeline-for-management
evals.prompt: Make a one-pager for management explaining how our devflow pipeline in this repo takes an idea from brainstorm to shipped code. They have one minute. Visual please.
evals.expected_output: An explainer built from the repository itself, whose first screen gives the pipeline in one statement, a diagram of the stages, a few takeaways about what makes it safe, and what it means for managers. Facts come from the repository's files.
assertions: Read the repository (README and the pipeline skills) before writing, per the transcript
In the first screen of a 1280x800 window the reader sees an answer headline and a diagram of the pipeline, with the key takeaways directly below
Respects the one-minute brief: under about 700 words in total, and at most two pages or tabs
States what the pipeline means for management (a decision, benefit or risk)
Every stage on the page corresponds to a real part of the pipeline in the repository (no invented stages)
Shows the stages as a visual flow or sequence diagram
Technical terms (for example quality gate, code review) are explained in plain language
Every abbreviation is spelled out at its first appearance
Contains no invented numbers or claims that are not in the repository
No emoji used as icons or decoration
No horizontal overflow or overlapping text at 1280px and 400px widths
